pageSubtitle: Explore donor-level functional data across conditions using interactive filtering and visualization.
Designed for rapid hypothesis generation, not formal statistical testing.

step1.title: Define donor cohort
step1.titleInfo: Use metadata and range filters to define the analysis cohort before exploring functional signals.

step2.title: Functional feature plots
step2.titleInfo: Inspect response trajectories across stimulation windows for the currently filtered donors.
step2.subtitle: Time-series / stimulation response
step2.subtitleInfo: This panel emphasizes temporal dynamics, donor variability, and mean trend under stimulation.
step2.responseTypeInfo: Switch analytes to compare secretion profiles (e.g., INS, GCG, SST) under the same cohort filter.

step3.title: Explore trait distribution
step3.titleInfo: Review trait-level distribution changes after cohort filtering to identify outliers and subgroup shifts.

step5.title: Inspect donor metadata
step5.titleInfo: Audit donor-level rows and export the filtered table for downstream analysis.

rightPanel.aboutInfo: Background context for what functional data represents and how to interpret this page.
rightPanel.aboutBody: Functional data represents physiological responses (e.g., insulin secretion) measured across stimuli or time.
rightPanel.importantBody: This tool is designed for filtering and visualization, not statistical testing. For hypothesis validation, use downstream statistical pipelines.
whyUseItems: No need to process raw scRNA-seq or functional datasets
